definitions.explanation: A strong desire to achieve something significant. One's purpose or aim in life, especially regarding career, contribution to society, or personal growth.

definitions.gloss: goodwill; kind intention; gift (as token of appreciation)
definitions.explanation: A gesture of appreciation or goodwill. Also refers to a small gift or monetary offering as an expression of gratitude or respect.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}い{志|こころざし}を{持|も}って{働|はたら}いている。
{志|こころざし}を{同|おな}じくする{仲間|なかま}と{出会|であ}えた。
examples.english: I met comrades who share the same aspirations.

examples.japanese: お{志|こころざし}だけいただきます。
examples.english: I gratefully accept your kind intention (but decline the gift itself).

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{志|こころざし}を{持|も}つ (to have aspirations)
・{高|たか}い{志|こころざし} (high aspirations/ambitions)
・{志|こころざし}を{立|た}てる (to set one's goals/resolve)
・{志|こころざし}を{同|おな}じくする (to share the same aspirations)
・{志|こころざし}{半|なか}ばで (with one's goals unfulfilled)

SENSE 2 USAGE:
お{志|こころざし} is used politely when referring to someone's kind gesture or offering:
・お{志|こころざし}、ありがとうございます (Thank you for your kind gesture)
・This usage often appears in formal contexts like funerals or ceremonies

RELATED WORDS:
・{志望|しぼう} (aspiration, desire - often for career goals)
・{野心|やしん} (ambition - can have negative connotation)
・{抱負|ほうふ} (aspiration, resolution - often for new year)
